properties.description:
Filed by Alex (who:alex, GitHub alexsligar-pnnl) on 2026-09-28 against reflow2 0.70.0. A team of about 8 at his workplace is moving a 1,173-node design from one laptop to a shared deployment: a container on a managed Kubernetes cluster behind a reverse proxy and an OIDC identity provider. `--serve-shared` handles concurrency; the blocker is that `--http` has no authentication.

WHAT THEY BUILT INSTEAD: an OAuth proxy as the reverse proxy's forward-auth backend, two identity-provider clients (one using the device-authorization grant), claim mappers, and a script that runs the device flow and prints an `.mcp.json` fragment with a Bearer header. It works, but every developer re-pastes a token when it expires, and every hosting team would reinvent about 600 lines of wiring.

THE ASK:
(1) `--http-oidc-issuer` + `--http-audience`: validate the Bearer JWT (signature, iss, aud, exp) and return 401 otherwise.
(2) `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, plus `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` on the 401, so MCP clients discover the sign-in and do it themselves.
(3) Optionally `--http-required-claim`.
Behaviour is unchanged when the flags are absent.

"THE PART I THINK YOU'LL ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT": "contributor_id is whatever the caller types, so on a shared graph any agent can sign as any contributor, and nothing in reflow2 can tell." A verified claim would let reflow2 derive the contributor and reject or flag a contributor_id that disagrees. Their proxy forwards X-Auth-Request-User "into a server that ignores it".

HOSTING NOTES:
· Mount the PARENT of the store, or the sidecars fall outside the volume and "the design silently comes up looking empty".
· Use a StatefulSet, because a rolling Deployment runs two pods and the second cannot take the lock.
· --http-allow-host is mandatory behind a proxy, and "its absence presents as a broken ingress rather than as a rejected Host header".

Registered and PARKED under dec:a-dated-field-report-is-registered-and-parked, and triaged under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. A public issue on the public repository, so nothing here is private. The employer is still left out of the records, as with other workplace reports.
properties.name: GitHub issue #616 (Alex, 2026-09-28): support OAuth 2.0 bearer-token auth natively, so reflow2 is an MCP protected resource, and attribute writes to a verified claim
